text: Git branching is a powerful feature in version control. Instead of working directly on the main codebase, developers create separate *feature branches* to work on new functions or fixes. This keeps the main branch stable and avoids conflicts. Once the work on a branch is complete, the developer merges it back into the main branch. Often, this is done through a *pull request*, which allows team members to review the changes before they are combined. This workflow makes collaboration easier, as multiple people can work on different features simultaneously. It also keeps a clear history of all changes, making it simpler to track bugs or roll back to an earlier version if needed.
